description: VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. A vector against itself is exactly 1.0, not 0.9999999999999999, and the [1,2,3]/[4,5,6] pair is 0.9746318461970762. INT operands do not change the answer: the VECTOR(INT,3) pair returns the identical double. The distinguishing property of the family is that float32 ELEMENTS feed float64 ARITHMETIC - over [0.1,0.2,0.3] and [0.4,0.5,0.6] the account returns 0.9746318467275483, the value obtained by widening the float32 elements and accumulating in float64, where the exact-decimal answer would be 0.9746318461970762. A zero-magnitude operand is NaN rather than an error: the divide by zero is not guarded. A TYPED NULL operand gives SQL NULL, while a dimension mismatch, mixed element types, a plain ARRAY and an untyped NULL are all compile errors naming both argument types - and because the check is COMPILE-time it fires over an empty table too. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorCosineSimilarityTest (now retired). The Java's assertFloat64 compared Java doubles; each converted case pins the full rendered double AND asserts equality against the literal in SQL, so neither a display truncation nor a widened comparison can hide a wrong answer. NaN is read through TO_VARCHAR, and the Java's assertRejected, which only asserted that something threw, becomes the exact live message.
